source.title: Hyperdimensional Probe: Decoding LLM Representations via Vector Symbolic Architectures
source.authors: Marco Bronzini; Carlo Nicolini; Bruno Lepri; Jacopo Staiano; Andrea Passerini

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains SAEs on LLM representations and evaluates their recovery of target concepts and the composition of extracted concepts. This bears on the SAE-feature branch of V4, using a different method and measures from the original toy-model superposition work.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and discusses SAE features, but does not test feature superposition geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or feature importance. Rows are limited to the paper's own SAE recovery and composition results; claims about prior work and VSA-only results are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper proposing a VSA-based probe. SAEs appear only as a comparison baseline, trained by the authors on k-means-pooled, sum-pooled multi-layer embeddings rather than a single residual-stream layer. SAE neurons are named by DLA top-10 tokens with fuzzy matching, and there is no chance or permuted baseline for SAE precision@k. The SAE numbers therefore show how a competing method performs on the authors' bounded analogy task. They do not test whether LLMs contain sparse features a dictionary can recover (V4), and no other version is examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The main conclusion is that LLM latent features can be faithfully captured with VSA representations, and that the hyperdimensional probe unifies probe, SAE and logit perspectives. They find it gives deeper, less variable findings than DLA and cleaner results than SAEs in bounded concept spaces. It also reveals model- and domain-specific concept compositionality and distinct QA failure sources (Llama losing question focus, GPT-2 having shallow representations). The SAE noisiness point is a secondary comparison claim.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition: it trains SAEs on LLM residual-stream embeddings and evaluates concept retrieval and composition, without testing toy-network superposition geometry or sparsity-dependent transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE retrieval differs between top-10 and top-100 activations; results also vary across the six LLMs. The paper notes that the choice of k can influence evaluations.

fits_no_version.finding: Paper-trained top-k SAEs on pooled LLM embeddings, with DLA-based naming, surface the target analogy concept in top-100 neurons (0.40–0.93) but often only out-of-context concepts in top-10 (up to 83.9% for GPT-2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In bounded task-oriented concept spaces, SAE features named via logit projection are noisy and k-dependent relative to a supervised VSA probe.

record.problems: The SAE comparison uses a shallow, paper-trained SAE with top-k sparsity set to 2%; feature naming relies on DLA and fuzzy token-to-concept matching. The authors note that the top-k choice affects evaluation and that SAE features can be noisy and lack task-aligned filtering. The paper does not establish that its extracted concepts are complete, stable, or canonical.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise qualifying SAE target-retrieval or composition results were left out. SAE reconstruction cosine scores are not rows because they measure reconstruction rather than recovery of features named by the claim.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no capacity or importance analysis of neurons.
All: no analysis of causes of polysemantic neurons.
No measure of features spread across neurons. No controlled test of SAE feature recovery; SAEs are only a comparison baseline.
All: no test of SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicality.
All: no test of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification and the V4 labels are dropped. The SAE is a baseline the authors built (4x latent, top-k 2%, pooled multi-layer input), and its precision@k has no chance control; the paper's controls (permuted and unrelated baselines) apply only to VSA. No version receives a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No test of toy networks with more features than dimensions, overlapping directions, transition geometry, or sparsity-dependent organization.
No test of polysemantic neurons as a consequence of capacity competition or of importance determining dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE-based concept recovery from LLM embeddings; does not test whether features are spread across many neurons.
No test of SAE-feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Llama 4, Scout
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated target-concept retrieval among the top-10 most strongly activated SAE neurons.
rows.note: SAE features were named using top-10 tokens from induced logit distributions and fuzzy token-to-concept matching.
rows.check: This is a comparison-method score, not a test of V4. Precision@10 depends on k, uses fuzzy matching of 100 logit tokens, and has no SAE chance baseline.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Top-100 SAE activations across the six tested LLMs
reader_labels.reason: SAE-based retrieval recovers target concepts, with precision@100 from 0.402 to 0.926 across models (r7–r12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Top-10 SAE activations and compositional extraction in the analogy task
reader_labels.reason: Top-10 retrieval varies substantially across models, and the top-10 composition results include high out-of-context-only shares for several models (r1–r6, r13–r18).
